facts.statement: Sequiwaimanu is an extinct genus of early penguin found in the Waipara Greensand of New Zealand.
facts.quote: Sequiwaimanu (meaning "to follow Waimanu") is an extinct genus of early penguin from the Waipara Greensand of New Zealand.

facts.statement: The type species Sequiwaimanu rosieae was named and described by Gerald Mayr in 2018.
facts.quote: The type species, S. rosieae, was named and described by Gerald Mayr in 2018.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered within the Claremont Estate, which was owned by Richard Goord at the time.
facts.quote: The specimen was discovered within Claremont Estate, which was owned by Richard Goord at the time of its discovery.

facts.statement: Sequiwaimanu lived between 61.66 and 56 million years ago during the Selandian to Thanetian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Thanetian (61.66 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sequiwaimanu belongs to the parent group Sphenisciformes.
Sequiwaimanu possessed leg bones that were similar to those of an unnamed giant penguin.
facts.quote: Sequiwaimanu had leg bones similar to an unnamed giant penguin.

rejected.statement: Sequiwaimanu is the fourth penguin species discovered from the Waipara Greensand in New Zealand.
rejected.quote: Sequiwaimanu is the fourth penguin species to be discovered from the Waipara Greensand in New Zealand.
